statements.t: In addition to Upgrade Energy’s California facility, we expect to open a battery manufacturing facility in Orlando, Florida in either December or January.

We expect our revenue to continue to grow as we continue to build out our capacity including our manufacturing facilities and products and significantly increasing our manufacturing staff to handle additional demand from the market.

Our gross profit is entirely driven based on our growth in top line revenue, while the decrease in margins is driven primarily by our continued and rapid expansion of manufacturing, however, we believe our margins are still within normal operating limits and will continue to increase as our manufacturing process continues to mature.

We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase as we continue to increase our infrastructure with additional hires, systems and processes, and as we become subject to additional compliance related activities.
We also anticipate professional fees and other expenses related to being a public company to increase.
In addition, we anticipate our non-cash stock compensation expense to be higher in 2026.
We do not anticipate our general and administrative expenses to increase at the same rate as our revenue as we start to gain operational efficiencies at scale.
We anticipate our gross margin to fluctuate period to period depending on certain promotions and products that are sold during the period and the mix of retail and enterprise sales during the period.
We expect our operations expense to increase as we continue to hire additional staff to support our operations including engineering staff to help improve process and gain efficiencies.

We anticipate additional operating expenses in the fourth quarter as we set up additional battery facilities with the completion of the Upgrade Energy acquisition and look to continue to expand additional operations including anew Orlando, Florida battery manufacturing facility in December or January.

We anticipate our sales and marketing costs to increase in 2026 related to expanding our enterprise sales team, however, we expect these increases to be at a lower rate than our revenue and other expenses as our enterprise sales are more dedicated efforts, while our retail revenue is driven off of advertising sales.
We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase as we continue to build out our infrastructure with additional hires and systems.
In addition, we anticipate our non-cash stock compensation expense to be higher in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Our future cash flows from operating activities will be significantly impacted by revenues received, our investment in sales and marketing to drive growth, and general and administrative expenses related to operating a public company.
Our ability to meet future liquidity needs will be driven by our operating performance and the extent of continued investment in our operations.

All three of these initiatives are well underway, and we expect they will contribute meaningful revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026 and throughout 2027.
While I believe GAAP results may partially obfuscate actual financial performance, we remain on track with an adjusted EBITDA loss of approximately $0.7 million for the quarter.
We expect customer concentration to generally increase through 2027 as the market consolidates around a smaller number of winners in different drone categories.
We will continue to build the systems and scale to meet the needs of both our commercial and defense partners until market signals suggest anything but overwhelming demand.
We are highly engaged with these partners and believe these represent long-term strategic relationships that will benefit Unusual Machines by providing deep market insights.

We have strong partnerships and supplier relationships with Powerus and Xtend, and we expect those investments to also drive meaningful revenue over the coming years as those companies win more business.
We will continue to scale production as quickly as possible, including adding a new automated motor production line expected to support 100,000 additional motors per month once fully operational.
We are on track to add domestic camera manufacturing in early 2027.

However, macroeconomic factors could reduce investment capital in the market, so we must stay disciplined and effectively manage margins and cash flow to avoid putting undue pressure on working capital as we scale.
We will work toward our 40% margin target, but achieving it may take longer as we prioritize rapid growth while managing losses.
We also continue to add product categories, such as batteries and additive manufacturing, and expect to continue expanding operations to meet demand.
We are pursuing continued growth and expect we will not be demand-limited through 2027.
